criticality_method.description: A-Mab uses a 'continuum of criticality' (per ICH Q9) rather than a binary Critical/Non-Critical designation. Criticality = impact on safety and efficacy combined with the certainty (uncertainty) of the knowledge used to establish that impact. Three tools are used. Tool #1 (Risk Ranking): Criticality (Risk Score) = Impact x Uncertainty; Impact scored on efficacy/biological activity, PK/PD, immunogenicity, and safety (highest of the four categories sets overall impact); scores multiplied; risk scores range 2 to 140. Tool #2 (Preliminary Hazards Analysis, PHA): Criticality (Risk Priority Number, RPN) = Severity x Likelihood; RPN range 1 to 81. Tool #3 (safety assessment for non-bioactive process components): Impurity Safety Factor, ISF = LD50 / Level in Product Dose (ISF > 1000 = minimal safety risk). Tools #1 and #2 do NOT account for process/manufacturing capability or detectability. Scales for Tool #1 (impact 2-20, uncertainty 1-7) were deliberately chosen so impact outweighs uncertainty. Criticality levels assigned: very low (VL), low (L), moderate (M), high (H), very high (VH); H and VH attributes are termed 'Critical'. Source pages 28-34, 54-55.
criticality_method.criticality_definition: Criticality is defined in the case study as impact on safety and efficacy; assessed as a continuum. Tool #1 Risk Score = Impact x Uncertainty; Tool #2 RPN = Severity x Likelihood; Tool #3 ISF = LD50/Level in Product Dose. High (H) and Very High (VH) = Critical. (pages 28, 33, 54)
criticality_method.severity_scale: Tool #1 Impact scale (score): Very High=20, High=16, Moderate=12, Low=4, None=2 (assessed across biological activity/efficacy, PK/PD, immunogenicity, safety; highest category sets overall impact) [Table 2.3, p32]. Tool #2 Severity scale (score): Very high=9 (death, microbiology infections, hypersensitivity), High=7 (cancer progression from lower efficacy or serious immunogenicity), Moderate=5, Low=3, Very low=1 (no measurable impact) [Table 2.5, p34].
criticality_method.uncertainty_scale: Tool #1 Uncertainty scale for variants/host-related impurities (score): 7=Very High (no information/new variant), 5=High (published external literature for variant in related molecule), 3=Moderate (nonclinical/in vitro data with this molecule or data from similar class), 2=Low (variant present in clinical trial material), 1=Very Low (impact established in clinical studies with this molecule) [Table 2.4, p32]. A separate process-raw-material uncertainty scale exists (7=no info, 3=component used in previous processes, 1=GRAS or studied in clinical trials). Tool #2 uses Likelihood instead (score): 9=Very high, 7=High, 5=Moderate, 3=Low, 1=Very low/never observed; conservative score >=5 when limited clinical data [Table 2.6, p34].

cqas.name: Aggregation (aggregates / HMW; includes fragments/LMW via same tests)
cqas.definition: Aggregated forms of A-Mab (mostly dimer); primary concern is enhanced immunogenicity potential; also potential effect on binding to Lymph-1, Fc and FcRn receptors and on PK. Detected by HPSEC, gel electrophoresis, analytical ultracentrifugation, HPSEC-MALLS (these tests also detect fragments/LMW). Purified A-Mab dimer had biological activity similar to monomer.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 0-5% aggregate; clinical experience 1-3% aggregate; range of experience 1-5% at end of shelf life with X-Mab. 5% upper range based on prior clinical experience with X-Mab. (Tables 2.7, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: High (H) - considered a Critical Quality Attribute (marked * in Table 2.28). Tool #1 Risk Score = 60 (H); Tool #2 RPN = 25 (M).
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 12 (Moderate, based on PK/PD); overall highest-category score drives Risk Score 60. Tool #2 Severity = 5 (Moderate).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 5 (High; published external literature for PK). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream / production culture (formation)
Low pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6) - lower pH may enhance aggregation
Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7) - reduces aggregate to acceptable levels; impacted by protein load, elution stop collect, elution pH, input aggregate
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - aggregate slightly impacted by Equilibration/Wash 1 conductivity and peak collection

cqas.name: Fragments / Low Molecular Weight (LMW) species
cqas.definition: Fragmentation products detected together with aggregates by HPSEC, gel electrophoresis, analytical ultracentrifugation and HPSEC-MALLS (listed as detecting 'fragments, aggregates'). Fragmentation is listed among typical mAb quality attributes (Table 2.2).
cqas.acceptance_or_target: not stated (no separate acceptable range given for fragments; assessed under aggregation/size-variant testing)
cqas.criticality: not stated as a separate scored attribute (fragmentation listed as a typical QA in Table 2.2 but not individually risk-ranked in Table 2.28)
impacted_by_steps: Detected by size-variant methods used across Protein A, CEX, AEX and virus filtration steps

cqas.name: Galactose Content / Galactosylation (%G0, %G1, %G2)
cqas.definition: N-linked complex biantennary oligosaccharide at Asn in constant region of each heavy chain; G2 = both arms terminal galactose (max 2 mol gal/mol HC), G1 = one arm, G0 = no terminal galactose. Extent of galactose does NOT affect ADCC but significantly affects CDC (fully agalactosylated G0 gave 25% decrease, fully galactosylated G2 gave 50% increase in CDC vs control). Assessed separately for %G0, %G1, %G2.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 10-40% (clinical experience 10-30% G0); 0-100% has statistical correlation with CDC activity. Based on Y-Mab prior knowledge (10-40% G0) plus A-Mab clinical experience. (Tables 2.9, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: High (H) - Critical Quality Attribute (marked *). Tool #1 Risk Score = 48 (H); Tool #2 RPN = 35 (H).
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 16 (High, on efficacy via CDC). Tool #2 Severity = 7 (High, based on CDC).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 3 (Moderate; in vitro data with this molecule). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor (primary determinant)
Minimally impacted by downstream processing (Protein A, CEX, AEX do not discriminate galactosylation variants); therefore excluded from downstream characterization

cqas.name: Afucosylation (core fucosylation)
cqas.definition: Extent of core afucosylation of the Fc glycan; inversely correlates with ADCC activity (fucose-deficient IgG1 has enhanced ADCC and improved FcgammaRIIIA binding). ADCC is the primary mechanism of action for A-Mab. A-Mab with 2-13% afucosylation gave a linear ADCC correlation spanning 70-130% activity.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 2-13% afucosylation (correlates with 70-130% ADCC); clinical experience 5-10% (Phase II/III); prior knowledge 1-11% (X-Mab, Y-Mab). Lower end covered by prior knowledge, upper end by modeled material (15%, no significant difference from 5%) in animal model. (Tables 2.9, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: High (H) - Critical Quality Attribute (marked *). Tool #1 Risk Score = 60 (H); Tool #2 RPN = 35 (H). (Early-development score would have been 10 if ADCC not yet known as MOA.)
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 20 (Very High, on efficacy via ADCC). Tool #2 Severity = 7 (High, ADCC dependence).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 3 (Moderate; in vitro data with this molecule). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor (primary determinant)
Minimally impacted by downstream processing; excluded from downstream characterization

cqas.name: High Mannose Content
cqas.definition: High mannose oligosaccharide forms, which are afucosylated and expected to significantly impact biological activity (ADCC); impact assigned same as afucosylation due to afucosylated nature.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 3-10% (clinical experience with A-Mab 3-10%). (Tables 2.9, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: Very High (VH) - Critical Quality Attribute (marked *). Tool #1 Risk Score = 80 (VH); Tool #2 RPN = 35 (H).
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 16 (High, on efficacy via ADCC). Tool #2 Severity = 7 (High).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 5 (High; literature/external data). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor (primary determinant)
Minimally impacted by downstream processing

cqas.name: Non-Glycosylated Heavy Chain
cqas.definition: Non-glycosylated Fc forms; non-glycosylated mAbs are not ADCC competent (Tao 1989), so impact on efficacy assigned same as afucosylation.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 0-3% (clinical experience with A-Mab 0-3%). (Tables 2.9, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: Very High (VH) - Critical Quality Attribute (marked *). Tool #1 Risk Score = 80 (VH); Tool #2 RPN = 35 (H).
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 16 (High, on efficacy via ADCC). Tool #2 Severity = 7 (High).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 5 (High; literature data). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor (primary determinant)
Minimally impacted by downstream processing

cqas.name: Sialic Acid Content / Sialylation
cqas.definition: Sialylated glycan forms; higher sialylation can reduce ADCC activity and impart anti-inflammatory properties. A narrow range (0-2%) on A-Mab showed no detectable impact on FcgammaRIIIa binding or ADCC. Present only at very low levels in A-Mab.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 0-2% (in vitro studies with A-Mab; clinical experience 0-0.2%, Phase II/III). (Tables 2.9, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: High per Tool #1 (marked * as Critical) but Moderate per Tool #2. Tool #1 Risk Score = 60 (H); Tool #2 RPN = 21 (M). Considered not critical to product quality in downstream discussion due to very low levels.
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 12 (Moderate, on efficacy). Tool #2 Severity = 7 (High).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 5 (High; published external literature). Tool #2 Likelihood = 3 (Low).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor
Charge-based steps (CEX, AEX) can discriminate sialylated structures, but sialylation levels are very low in A-Mab

cqas.name: Host Cell Protein (HCP)
cqas.definition: CHO host cell proteins; primary concern is potential for immunogenicity (based on X-Mab). Measured by HCP assay (ELISA). X-Mab high-HCP material showed no difference in potency or FcRn binding.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range 0-100 ng/mg (clinical experience 5-20 ng/mg); prior knowledge up to 3600 ng/kg (120 ng/mg) in X-Mab Phase I. 100 ng/mg upper limit based on prior X-Mab clinical experience. (Tables 2.15, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: Moderate to High (M-H) - considered a Critical Quality Attribute (marked *). Tool #1 Risk Score = 36 (M-H); Tool #2 RPN = 15 (M).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 3 (Moderate; data from similar class of molecule, X-Mab). Tool #2 Likelihood = 3 (Low).
impacted_by_steps: Protein A Affinity Chromatography (Step 5) - removes HCP
Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7) - reduces HCP; impacted by protein load, wash conductivity, input HCP
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - removes HCP; impacted by Equilibration/Wash 1 buffer conductivity and AEX load pH

cqas.name: Residual DNA (host cell DNA)
cqas.definition: Host cell (CHO) DNA; theoretical risk is oncogene transfer. Platform DNA is typically <60 bp (low oncogene-transfer risk). Y-Mab DNA spike at WHO limit showed no impact on potency or FcRn binding. WHO recommends <10 ng DNA/dose.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Claimed acceptable range less than 10^-3 ng/dose; A-Mab DNA size typically <60 bp. (Table 2.17)
cqas.criticality: Very Low (VL). Tool #1 Risk Score = 6 (VL); Tool #2 RPN = 1 (VL).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 3 (Moderate; prior knowledge with similar molecule). Tool #2 Likelihood = 1 (Very low/never observed).
impacted_by_steps: Protein A Affinity Chromatography (Step 5) - removal of DNA
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - removes DNA (also cleared by CEX). Clearance capability very high; minimal product-specific data needed (modular claim)

cqas.name: Leached Protein A
cqas.definition: Protein A (S. aureus cell wall protein) leached from the affinity column; binds Fc domain and could impact efficacy/PK; potentially immunogenic and mitogenic. Not all leached Protein A is intact. Primate doses up to 1 mg/kg well tolerated; PROSORBA medical use shows no adverse events from leachate.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: No range claimed due to low to moderate criticality (Protein A is always cleared from the process). (Table 2.19)
cqas.criticality: Low (Tool #1) to Moderate (Tool #2) - low to moderate criticality. Tool #1 Risk Score = 16 (L); Tool #2 RPN = 15 (M).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 1 (Very Low; studied in clinical trials, process raw material scale). Tool #2 Likelihood = 3 (Low).
impacted_by_steps: Protein A Affinity Chromatography (Step 5) - source of leached Protein A
Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7) - clearance
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - removes Protein A to drug substance acceptance levels

cqas.name: Methotrexate (MTX)
cqas.definition: Cytotoxic DHFR inhibitor used in early seed cultures to maintain selective pressure (not in production cultures). 'Black Box Warning' for bone marrow, liver, lung, kidney toxicities (dose/frequency related, mostly reversible). Assessed with Tool #1 and Tool #3 (ISF).
cqas.acceptance_or_target: No range claimed due to low criticality (MTX always cleared from process). ISF calculation: TME 0.0000443 mg/kg, LD50 6 mg/kg, ISF = 135,000 (Table 2.23); overall Table 2.28 lists ISF 268000. ISF >1000 = minimal safety risk. (Tables 2.21, 2.22, 2.23, 2.28)
cqas.criticality: Low to Moderate. Tool #1 Risk Score = 16 (L, driven by safety); Tool #3 ISF >1000 (minimal safety risk). Tool #2 not determined (ND).
cqas.severity: Tool #1 Impact = 16 (High, safety - reversible AEs). Tool #2 severity not determined.
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 1 (Very Low; studied in clinical trials, process raw material scale).
impacted_by_steps: Used in seed culture expansion (Steps 1-2, early seed cultures)
Cleared through downstream purification (high clearance capability; modular claim, minimal product-specific data)

cqas.name: C-terminal Lysine (Truncation) - basic charge variant
cqas.definition: C-terminal lysine post-translational modification/truncation (0-Lys, 1-Lys, 2-Lys distribution); a basic charge variant. Detected by ion exchange chromatography, isoelectric focusing, peptide mapping-MS. Purified variants equally potent; 1-Lys converts to 0-Lys in serum within 6 hours (predominant circulating form is 0-Lys). Assessment applies to IV administration.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: No range claimed due to low criticality. A-Mab distribution: 87.4±2.3% 0-Lys, 11.2±1.8% 1-Lys, 1.4±0.8% 2-Lys. (Tables 2.24, 2.26)
cqas.criticality: Very Low (VL). Tool #1 Risk Score = 4 (VL); Tool #2 RPN = 1 (VL).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 2 (in vitro/clinical data with this molecule; Table 2.28 lists uncertainty 2). Tool #2 Likelihood = 1 (Very low).
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture (cell-culture-process dependent, per X-Mab Process I vs II)
Converted to 0-Lys in serum post-administration (biological, not a manufacturing step)

cqas.name: Deamidated Isoforms (Deamidation) - acidic charge variant
cqas.definition: Deamidation at Asn/Gln residues (primary site Asn-A in Fc; also Asn-B, Asn-C at lower levels); an acidic charge variant. Sites are not in CDRs nor in Fc region affecting effector function, so no effect on biological activity; occurs naturally in human plasma (25-77% over 5 weeks) with retained binding/activity; no PK difference in rat study; no immunogenicity in cyno study. Detected by IEC, IEF, peptide mapping-MS.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: No range claimed due to low criticality (18-24% range of experience); included as a measure of process consistency in characterization studies. (Tables 2.11, 2.29)
cqas.criticality: Very Low (Tool #1) to Low (Tool #2). Tool #1 Risk Score = 4 (VL); Tool #2 RPN = 9 (L).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 2 (Table 2.28; nonclinical/clinical data with this molecule). Tool #2 Likelihood = 3 (Low).
impacted_by_steps: Low pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6) - lower pH/temperature can change charge variant profile
Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7) - acidic species slightly impacted by protein load; acidic variants elute at front of peak
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - acidic species slightly impacted by load pH

cqas.name: Oxidation (methionine)
cqas.definition: Oxidation of heavy chain Met-250 and Met-420 (susceptible to tert-butyl hydroperoxide). Residues not within Fcgamma receptor epitopes, so no expected ADCC impact (confirmed comparable potency when fully oxidized). Met-420->Leu had minor (<20%) FcRn effect (low potential PK impact). Oxidized A-Mab could lead to aggregation, increasing immunogenicity potential. Detected by peptide mapping-MS.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: No range claimed due to low criticality. (Table 2.13)
cqas.criticality: Low (Tool #1) to Moderate (Tool #2). Tool #1 Risk Score = 12 (L); Tool #2 RPN = 25 (M).
cqas.uncertainty: Tool #1 Uncertainty = 3 (Moderate; laboratory data / similar class of molecule). Tool #2 Likelihood = 5 (Moderate).
impacted_by_steps: Process and storage related (not tied to a specific characterized unit operation in the case study)

cqas.name: Potency / Biological Activity (ADCC and CDC)
cqas.definition: A-Mab's mechanism of action is primarily ADCC (B-cell killing primarily through ADCC; CDC activity cannot be ruled out as part of MOA). Potency/bioactivity is the functional efficacy attribute against which glycosylation variants are assessed: afucosylation, high mannose, non-glycosylated HC and galactose all modulate ADCC (afuco 2-13% -> 70-130% ADCC) or CDC (galactose 0-100% correlates with CDC). Potency assay used to test aggregate, deamidated, oxidized, C-terminal lysine and other variants.
cqas.acceptance_or_target: not stated as a single numeric release spec in Chapter 2; ADCC range 70-130% correlated with 2-13% afucosylation; CDC increases with galactose (G0 = -25%, G2 = +50% vs control). (pages 37-42)
cqas.criticality: Critical as the efficacy endpoint - drives criticality of the ADCC/CDC-linked glycosylation CQAs (afucosylation H, galactose H, high mannose VH, non-glyc HC VH). Not separately scored in Table 2.28.
cqas.severity: Efficacy is the highest-weighted impact category in Tool #1 (Impact up to 20 = Very High) and Tool #2 severity (up to 7-9).
cqas.uncertainty: not stated as a separate score
impacted_by_steps: Upstream production culture / bioreactor (determines glycosylation and thus ADCC/CDC)
Downstream steps do not modify glycosylation, so potency largely set upstream

cqas.name: Adventitious Virus / Viral Safety (viral clearance)
cqas.definition: Adventitious virus and endogenous retrovirus-like particles potentially present in mammalian (CHO) cell culture; an in-process safety attribute that cannot be detected in final product, so control relies on process design (dedicated inactivation/removal steps). In-process quality attributes include Bioburden, MMV, Mycoplasma, Adventitious Virus. Model viruses: XMuLV (large, enveloped) and MVM (small, non-enveloped parvovirus).
cqas.acceptance_or_target: Total viral log reduction: >16.7 (XMuLV) and >8.6 (MVM). Per-step LRF: Low pH inactivation >6.6 (XMuLV); Anion Exchange >5.5 (XMuLV) / >4.0 (MVM); Small Virus Retentive Filtration >4.6 / >4.6. (Table on p165)
cqas.criticality: Critical for safety; controlled by process design because it cannot be detected in final product (per Figure 6.1 rationale). Not scored via Tool #1/#2 in Table 2.28 (managed via viral clearance risk assessment, Chapter 4).
cqas.severity: Very high (viral safety maps to death/microbiology-related infections; Tool #2 severity anchor = 9). Assessed via dedicated viral clearance / modular claims rather than product-variant tools.
cqas.uncertainty: Managed by modular viral clearance approach leveraging prior knowledge across multiple antibodies (no additional spiking studies needed for low-pH treatment).
impacted_by_steps: Low pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6) - inactivates enveloped viruses
Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8) - virus removal
Small Virus Retentive Filtration (Step 9) - removes small parvoviruses (MVM) and larger viruses (MuLV)
cqas.source_pages: 112 (in-process attributes), 113-114 (Table 4.1), 117 (Table 4.3 model viruses), 152-166 (viral clearance, LRF table p165), 236-238 (Figure 6.1 rationale)
